summary: Focused participant deadline and gate changes pass the local emulator suite. Existing authorization and private-data issues prevent a full production security sign-off. These are static-code findings; no production exploitation or account changes were attempted.

findings.issue: The existing isPortalAdminAccount helper trusts any authenticated email matching portal-admin\..*@firebase\.app without email_verified or binding to the established administrator UID. That identity can bootstrap an admin user document. This predates the event change.
findings.recommendation: Migrate the established administrator to a server-managed claim or pinned verified identity. Retain access for the existing administrator through a coordinated migration; do not silently create or reset accounts.

findings.issue: Approved staff can read submissions globally, and judge-map ownership validation does not establish event-assignment isolation. UI event selection alone is not a database authorization boundary.
findings.recommendation: Enforce trusted event assignments in read and scoring rules, validate the associated queries, and cover cross-event denials without breaking legacy assignments.

findings.issue: The existing users rules allow signed-in readers to read participant documents containing emails and profile fields; private judge notes also share a submission document readable by its owner and teammates.
findings.recommendation: Separate public profile snapshots, private account data and judge-only notes into documents with appropriate ownership and staff access.

findings.check: Type Safety / Business Logic vs. Rules
findings.issue: Dynamic criterion-specific bounds and Osaka's automatic ai-video assignment are handled in the normal client flow; the existing rules do not validate every configured criterion key, weight or track membership. Score-map ownership tests do not prove full scoring-value integrity.
findings.recommendation: Add server-authoritative submission and scoring validation tied to the saved event rubric and track catalog, with tests for direct SDK bypasses.
